The short version

A rich, sweet sherry-cask Canadian blend with good evidence for texture and persistence, but moderate complexity. Its original and reoffer prices are kept distinct.

Exact identity: Pike Creek 22 Year Pedro Ximénez / PX Cask Finish, 2021-introduced limited range reoffered in 2024, 45% ABV / 90 proof, 750 mL.

Background and history

Original 2021 release is documented by the dated launch record and independent account. Producer catalogue publication November 26, 2024 records a later reoffer, not the first launch.

Historical CAD 90 review context is distinct from the checked current CAD 199.95 producer offer. Awards are supporting identity records, not numerical Quality inputs.

For the shared historical context, read Canadian whisky, cross-border trade and the American market. The release chronology above distinguishes the current bottle from its brand’s earlier history.

Producer, grains, aging and finishing

Producer verifies twenty-two years, 45%, corn/rye and sweet Pedro Ximénez sherry casks. Complete initial cask history and finish duration are not authenticated. The old original November 2021 review and 2024 catalogue reoffer share the exact named age/finish, but recipe continuity across batches is not independently proven. A twenty-one-year Oloroso predecessor is not this twenty-two-year PX expression.

Critical review synthesis

Kurt Bradley · The Gentleman’s Flavor

Bradley finds a creamy/syrupy palate, complementary dark-fruit/sweetness and a medium-long warm ending. He calls it very pleasant but not highly complex.

Scope: Original 2021-introduced twenty-two-year / 45% range; page updated May 2023, exact tasting day unspecified. Current-batch identity limits explicit.

Judging panel · World Whiskies Awards

The exact 2022 entry describes a notably sweet palate, developed fruit/nut/grain notes and lingering sweetness, with unusual leafy/polish-like aromatic detail.

Scope: 2022 exact twenty-two-year / 45% PX entry; paraphrased sensory account, no award-to-score conversion.

Published sample evidence, not first-person tasting or a representative survey. Reviewer disagreement and recipe-era limitations remain explicit; publisher grades are not mechanically converted.

Quality and calibration

Quality 7.1 / 10. Very good provisional Canadian blend execution. Creamy weight, complementary fruit/sweet development and a persistent warm finish have independent support. Moderate complexity and dominant sweetness constrain stronger claims; twenty-two years adds no points.

No defensible complete Canadian native 1/5/10 framework is established for this comparison group. Seven universal execution dimensions are assessed within Canadian Blended Whisky; unrelated American bourbon and straight-rye endpoints are not imported.

Calibration mode: evidence_limited_provisional. Evidence-limited provisional; matched independent tasting with sample and era limitations

Serving recommendations

Neat

Start with a small neat pour and assess development and texture against the attributed accounts.

Water / rocks

Add drops or one small cube gradually; compare texture before adding more dilution.

Old Fashioned

Taste before adding syrup, especially with sweet or wine-influenced expressions; recurring blends can be the cost comparison.

Manhattan / highball

Try a small serve with vermouth or soda, adjusting sweetness and dilution to the documented style.

Serving suggestions are editorial starting points, grounded in documented strength and style; adjust to your taste.
